propositions: Four AST structural guards emit false negatives because they pin ast.parse/inspect.getsource scans to hardcoded source files that no longer hold the policed constructs after module refactors
Each of the four vacuous guards (findings 1-4) was measured to contain zero instances of its policed construct in the scanned target module
Guards that survived prior relocations share a common pattern: an explicit anti-vacuity assertion paired with a coverage landmark proving the scan population is non-empty

The repair pattern requires deriving the scan population dynamically from module transitive closures instead of hardcoding filenames, adding anti-vacuity assertions with landmarks, and mutation-testing each repaired guard by re-introducing the policed construct at its real home
Finding 6 uses a relative pathlib.Path that breaks when pytest cwd is not the repo root; the fix anchors it to __file__
Findings 5, 7, 8 are either fixed with anti-vacuity assertions (F5) or accepted as non-vacuity issues with recorded rationale (F7, F8)
